subject: Oceanography
title: Shark Finning
description: A quick, practical guide to Shark Finning.

hook.text: 100 million sharks are killed each year—many just for their fins, with the body thrown back to the sea.

buildup.text: Shark fin soup is a delicacy in parts of Asia—a single fin can sell for hundreds of dollars.

discovery.text: Sharks are apex predators—their removal cascades through food webs, causing ecosystem-wide imbalances.

twist.text: Without sharks, ray populations explode—overgrazing shellfish beds, which then collapse.

climax.text: 71% of shark and ray species are now threatened with extinction—populations have declined 71% since 1970.

punchline.text: Killing the ocean's top predators unravels the web beneath them.

quiz.question: What ecological effect does removing sharks cause?
options: Cascading imbalances through the food web
